description: The overall HGB average is an average of patient averages, so each patient counts once.

c.request: Among patients whose average hemoglobin (`HGB`) across their lab records (ignoring missing values) is above the overall average hemoglobin, list the patient ID, their average HGB, how far it is above the overall average, and their average minus the average of these above-average patients' averages. Show the top 10 by that last value, highest first, unrounded. The overall HGB average is an average of patient averages, so each patient counts once.
c.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(HGB) IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) AS overall_avg_hgb FROM patient_averages), above_average AS (SELECT p.ID, p.avg_hgb, o.overall_avg_hgb FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE p.avg_hgb > o.overall_avg_hgb), above_average_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) AS mean_above_avg_hgb FROM above_average) SELECT a.ID AS patient_id, a.avg_hgb, a.avg_hgb - a.overall_avg_hgb AS above_overall_avg, a.avg_hgb - m.mean_above_avg_hgb AS above_average_patient_difference FROM above_average AS a CROSS JOIN above_average_mean AS m ORDER BY above_average_patient_difference DESC LIMIT 10;

a.request: For each patient ID in the Laboratory table, compute their average hemoglobin (`HGB`) over their lab records, ignoring missing values. Define the overall average as the mean of these per-patient averages, so every patient counts once no matter how many tests they had. Keep the patients whose average is above that overall average. For each kept patient, list the ID, their average HGB, how far it is above the overall average, and their average minus the mean of the kept patients' averages. Sort by that last value from highest to lowest and show the top 10, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) AS overall_avg FROM patient_averages), kept AS (SELECT p.ID, p.avg_hgb, o.overall_avg FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE p.avg_hgb > o.overall_avg), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) AS mean_kept_avg FROM kept) SELECT k.ID, k.avg_hgb, k.avg_hgb - k.overall_avg AS above_overall_avg, k.avg_hgb - m.mean_kept_avg AS above_kept_mean FROM kept AS k CROSS JOIN kept_mean AS m ORDER BY above_kept_mean DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: For each patient with at least one nonmissing HGB value, calculate their unrounded average HGB; average those patient averages to get the overall HGB average; keep patients whose average exceeds it; then return the top 10 by their average minus the average of the qualifying patients’ averages, descending, with patient ID, average HGB, amount above the overall average, and that final difference
b.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS average_hgb FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), overall AS (SELECT AVG(average_hgb) AS overall_average_hgb FROM patient_averages), qualifying AS (SELECT p.ID, p.average_hgb, p.average_hgb - o.overall_average_hgb AS amount_above_overall_average FROM patient_averages p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.average_hgb > o.overall_average_hgb), qualifying_average AS (SELECT AVG(average_hgb) AS average_qualifying_hgb FROM qualifying) SELECT q.ID AS patient_id, q.average_hgb, q.amount_above_overall_average, q.average_hgb - a.average_qualifying_hgb AS final_difference FROM qualifying q CROSS JOIN qualifying_average a ORDER BY final_difference DESC, q.ID LIMIT 10

d.request: Which 10 patients have the highest average HGB above the overall HGB average? Calculate each patient’s average from their non-missing lab records, then calculate the overall average from those patient averages so each patient counts once. For each patient, list their ID, average HGB, amount above the overall average, and difference between their average and the average of all above-average patients’ averages. Sort by the last difference, highest first, and leave all values unrounded.
d.sql: WITH patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS average_hgb FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), overall AS (SELECT AVG(average_hgb) AS overall_average FROM patient_averages), above_average AS (SELECT p.ID, p.average_hgb, o.overall_average FROM patient_averages AS p CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE p.average_hgb > o.overall_average), above_average_mean AS (SELECT AVG(average_hgb) AS mean_above_average FROM above_average) SELECT a.ID, a.average_hgb, a.average_hgb - a.overall_average AS amount_above_overall_average, a.average_hgb - m.mean_above_average AS difference_from_above_average_mean FROM above_average AS a CROSS JOIN above_average_mean AS m ORDER BY difference_from_above_average_mean DESC, a.ID LIMIT 10;
